opportunity.name: Printable Weekly Planner Templates
opportunity.target_customer: Students and professionals who plan on paper
opportunity.problem: Paper-planner users want inexpensive, printable layouts without buying a new physical planner each year.
opportunity.proposed_solution: A bundle of printable weekly layouts in A4 and US Letter.

facts_from_evidence.claim: Etsy charges a $0.20 listing fee per item, and a listing lasts four months.
Planner buyers ask for both A4 and US Letter printable sizes.
Etsy listing fee is $0.20 per listing.
Printable planners are a crowded Etsy category with many near-identical listings.
Forum poster: 'Etsy listing fees are $0.50 now, it is getting expensive.'
Forum poster: 'My planner shop made 40 sales in its first month with no advertising.'

market_research.customer_segment: Students and professionals who plan on paper

demand_indicators.note: Stages: none < general_interest < active_problem_awareness < purchase_consideration < verified_transactions. Search volume, views and likes can justify at most 'general_interest' (§10.3, §18.3).

tam.note: Insufficient verified evidence: a reliable TAM estimate cannot be established from the available evidence.

som.note: Insufficient verified evidence: a reliable SOM estimate cannot be established from the available evidence.

saturation.note: Saturation is assessed from recorded competitors and competitor evidence only; customer-acquisition difficulty rises with saturation and no differentiation may mean rejection (§29F).

competitor_analysis.comparison_note: Prices appear only where a pricing claim was recorded with evidence; competitor revenue, customer counts and market share are never estimated (§11.2).
competitor_analysis.differentiation_note: A recommendation must explain why customers would switch; 'competitors are expensive' is not sufficient (§11.4).

price_assumption.basis: stated assumption for a printable bundle

break_even.note: Break-even = ceil(recurring monthly costs / contribution per sale).

budget.note: Compatible means startup + first month recurring fits the owner's stated budget. The budget figure is the owner's; the engine never raises it (§13.6).

distribution.organic_traffic_assumption: not assumed — organic traffic must be earned and is not forecast (§14)
distribution.paid_advertising_assumption: not assumed profitable — no ad economics are claimed without cost evidence (§14)
distribution.note: Channel availability does not imply acquisition success; conversion requirements and acquisition cost remain unproven until real evidence exists.

commercial_feasibility.estimate_notice: All figures are deterministic calculations over caller-stated inputs classified per line (verified/quoted/historical/estimate/unknown). Estimated revenue is not verified revenue (§13.3).

compliance.note: Screening is a deterministic pattern check over declared fields; a 'clear' verdict is not a legal opinion (§15).
